title: Routing Logic

story.briefing: Power has to go somewhere. The junction in Sector 6 needs a rule for choosing a path, and it has to survive a reading that should never have reached it.
story.success: Junction reprogrammed. Power finds its way around the damage.

description: Given a power load and whether a backup line is available, decide the route. A negative load is invalid: return "INVALID". A load of 50 or less always goes to "PRIMARY". Above 50, use "BACKUP" when a backup line is available. When no backup is available, a load of 90 or less still goes to "PRIMARY", but anything above 90 must return "SHUTDOWN".

examples.explanation: The invalid check comes before everything else.

hints: Four outcomes, but they are not all at the same level. One condition overrides every other and should be tested first.
After the invalid check, the load splits into ranges, and only some of those ranges care about the backup line. Draw the four cases out before writing them.
Return "INVALID" for a negative load. Then return "PRIMARY" for 50 or less. For what remains, return "BACKUP" if a backup exists; otherwise return "PRIMARY" up to 90 and "SHUTDOWN" above it.
